items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

ctx.x: The state of jazz these days seems to have found its ways of course into universities and the academic world. Is that a good thing?

I knew you were going to ask me this. I’m going to be very honest. In some ways it is and in some ways — and this is only me and I’m not that important as far as my word but I speak but I feel — in some ways it is and in some ways it isn’t. In the ways that it is is it makes people aware of this wonderful music, which is American, which hopefully will close the gap between black and white, I hope. I’d like to see that happen. You play, you play. I don’t know, what color are you? I don’t know, is there a color…
